### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **72** documentable anchor(s).

**46** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **25** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `08170dc4334c80566044abb119169acdaac6028d` — the merge of head `011f9aa4e1e2eec190bc853140e051749387aba4` into base `7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 08170dc4334c80566044abb119169acdaac6028d && git checkout 08170dc4334c80566044abb119169acdaac6028d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4 011f9aa4e1e2eec190bc853140e051749387aba4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4 && git merge --no-ff 011f9aa4e1e2eec190bc853140e051749387aba4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7993aa76afc4e4cab80aaf5c813bce00e7e11bc4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `011f9aa4e1e2eec190bc853140e051749387aba4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/external-driver-errors.ts, packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.ts, packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-window-read.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-window-read.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/pull-refusal.ts + read, never reviewed: docs/adr/0153-one-way-sync-in-beside-federation.md (D1, D2, the children table), packages/core/src/utils/temporal-storage-form.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-automation/package.json, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json, AGENTS.md (the two declaration lines), .changeset/32062-sync-in-windowed-read.md

Rendered by an isolated sub-agent of this seat at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, from the card (body and all six comments), the PR body, its eight files, the net diff against `main` (merge base `7993aa76`) and the check-runs on this head. Read-only: nothing was built, run or re-run. The check-runs on the head are 35 `success` and 16 `skipped` (UI jobs, opt-in harnesses, queue verdicts, the live PG + MySQL temporal conformance job); none failed.

**Result: PASS, with one should-fix (④ S1) that earns a delta review of its fix, and five nits.**

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The floor's accept set is unchanged. Right.** `readCapped` in `external-driver-floor.ts` still throws on `rows.length` above the cap and on nothing else; the only change is a fourth constructor argument. No read that answered before is refused now, and none that was refused answers now.
2. **`ExternalRowCapExceededError` gains public surface, additively. Right.** The class is exported from the `@objectstack/objectql` root. It gains an optional fourth constructor argument (default `[]`), the getter `returnedRowCount` and the method `returnedValuesOf(field)`. `code`, `status`, `httpStatus` and `details` are byte-identical, so the wire shape is unchanged. The rows sit in a `#private` field, which no enumeration, spread, `JSON.stringify` or `structuredClone` reaches.
3. **The refusal's message changes. Right as a re-point, see nit N1.** "mirror the data into a real object with DataSync" becomes "copy the rows into a synced object with sync-in (a mapping whose datasourceSource names the object, pulled by a job)". This is the one change a caller can observe today.
4. **`ConnectorPullRefusalReason` gains five members. Right, additive.** `sync_window_unsplittable`, `sync_bounds_not_pushed`, `source_key_not_exact`, `watermark_not_exact`, `watermark_start_invalid`. The type is exported from the package root, so a consumer with an exhaustive switch over it gets a type error; no such consumer exists in this tree (`git grep` for an existing member finds only `connector-pull.ts` and `pull-refusal.ts`). The three tokens the spec child reserved are reused verbatim, as carrier note 6762989212 item 3 asks.
5. **The move of `ConnectorPullError` keeps one class and both export paths. Right.** `connector-pull.ts` re-exports it from `pull-refusal.ts`, and `index.ts` (untouched) still exports it from `connector-pull.js`. `mapping_name_refused` from #32117 is carried into the moved union at the same position.
6. **The reader is not public surface and has no caller. Right.** `datasource-window-read.ts` is imported only by its own test; `index.ts` does not export it. Its three runtime imports (`@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`) are declared `dependencies` of the package.
7. **Codes and statuses of the new refusals. Right.** The two floored refusals reuse `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP_EXCEEDED` / 422, the floor's own pair; the three value refusals use `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, the pair `no_connector_source` and its siblings already use.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — the card's line, carried unchanged on the PR body and the changeset. **This slice's diff, by itself, narrows nothing an author or a caller can reach today:**

- no schema, liveness row or build rule is touched (nothing under `packages/spec` differs from `main`);
- the floor refuses exactly the reads it refused before (① 1);
- the five new reasons are thrown only by a reader nothing calls (① 6).

So for this slice alone the accurate kind is `Metadata-protocol: none`, and what it publishes is additive surface (① 2 and 4). The lines over-declare, in the conservative direction, and the changeset body says so in words ("This slice narrows nothing on its own"). I judge that honest by disclosure and accept it as a deviation, nit N5: the declaration is what put this PR on the narrowing face and under the dogfood battery, and a slice that under-declared would be the error.

Level: `minor` on `@objectstack/objectql` and on `@objectstack/service-automation`. That is at or above what the diff publishes on each (new members on an exported class; new members on an exported union), and it is the level the declared kind takes. No major, nothing removed or renamed, so no migration table is owed. The ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) is true of this diff, and it commits the card's real narrowings (D8's `job.organization` under `group`, D3's incremental `mark` refusal) to the slices that enforce them, each with its own disposition. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report's four `open_questions` (6772367718) are each answered by the seat in 6773389044, as seat-discretion calls the maintainer may veto; none is a maintainer ruling and none is needed for this slice:

1. Pull-result contract: A (a source discriminator on `ConnectorSourcePullResult`). It binds slice 2, which then carries a published-schema face and its own review. Nothing in this diff depends on it.
2. The two `packages/spec` lines the ADR row names: A, they ride this card. Not in this diff.
3. Where `sys_sync_run` is registered: A, after #32073. **One thing to reconcile:** the seat's answer calls this "slice 5", while the PR body's slice order puts `sys_sync_run` in slice 2 together with the `job.pull` wiring. If the wiring waits with it, the reader stays dead and N1 stays true for longer. The seat should restate the order before slice 2 starts.
4. WARN lines while halving: A, leave it. Accepted; the lines carry `message` and `stack`, and the rows are in neither.

Dev flags:

- **Reader ships with no caller; no liveness row flips.** Correct for this slice. The ADR flips a `planned` row "with the reader that makes it true", and no door reaches this reader yet, so `datasourceSource` rightly stays `planned` under `authorWarn`.
- **Per-dialect client defaults NOT MEASURED** (Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle), deferred to slice 6. Accepted as declared: the ADR lists these as cases the engine child owes, the card stays open, and the run-time refusal is what protects a run until then. The live PG + MySQL conformance job is `skipped` on this head, which agrees with the declaration.
- **Stale "DataSync" comment in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`.** Carrier named by the seat (the slice that next touches the file). Accepted.
- Carrier note items: item 1 (a key undeclared at build) is covered at run time by the value check in `judgeRows`; item 3 is met (① 4). Items 2, 5, 6 and 7 belong to later slices and are untouched here.
- The stray `/lint.pid` outside the repository is the operator's; the worktree and trailer deviations change nothing in the tree.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself.** Read against D1, D2 and the children table on `main`, this slice takes no declared capability away at a consumer. The two floored refusals are the spec's own: D1 says a driver that pushes one bound or none "is refused under its own name", and D2 says one canon step over the cap refuses as `sync_window_unsplittable`. The run-time exactness refusals are invariant 7's last sentence ("a value that still comes back as a number outside the safe range refuses the run with the same reason"). `watermark_start_invalid` is not named by the ADR; it refuses a `start` that can bound no window, which D1's "the lowest value read" presupposes. Nothing here is a capability declared and then narrowed.

**Invariants read against the code** (`datasource-window-read.ts`):

- 3, 4, 5 hold. `range()` sends only `$gte` and `$lt` on spelled canon values. Every value read back goes through `canonOf`, which truncates (`temporalStorageForm` reads a finer fraction by truncation; `Math.floor` for integers). The page cursor is the key alone.
- 7 holds at run time: `judgeRows` runs before every `land`, on both paths.
- 8 holds: `commitWindow` is called only after `readPaged` returns or after one floored `find` has answered.
- 10 holds: every `find`, both high-water reads included, goes through `scoped()`.
- 12 holds. Built-in: bounded windows tile from `from` to `floor(H0)`. Floored: every bounded `hi` is at or below `V`, the largest value an over-cap answer showed.
- 9 holds on the main line: `min(maxWritten, H0)` on a multi-page bounded window (H0 is at or below the value the source held before that window, so it is the conservative reading of (b)), `min(maxWritten, H1)` on a multi-page open-above window, (a) alone on a single read. **It does not hold on one edge: S1.**
- 11 (the NULL count) is not implemented here and is not claimed; it is slice 4's.

**S1, should-fix: the open-above window's commit when the high-water read before it answers nothing, or answers below `from`.** `builtin()` passes `pages > 1 ? h1 : undefined` to `commitWindow`, and `commitWindow` reads `undefined` as "no cap".

- When `highWater()` finds no row (`h1` is `undefined`: the source held no non-NULL watermark under the scope) and the window is then read in more than one page, the commit is `maxWritten`, uncapped. That is the case (b) exists for. A row read on page one and updated while later pages are read moves to a value the next run must reach; rows with higher keys written after it push `maxWritten` above that value, and the update is not read again until a full pull. The source held nothing before the first page, so the safe commit is nothing, or `from`.
- When `h1` is defined but below `from` (the source's maximum sat below the committed position or below `watermark.start`, and more than a page of rows arrived during the read), the commit is `h1`, a position below where the run started. If `from` was `watermark.start`, the next run reads from below the value D1 calls "the lowest value read".

Both need rows to arrive in bulk during one run, so they are narrow, and nothing calls the reader yet; that is why this is not a must-fix. It is a hole in invariant 9 all the same. The fix is small: on a multi-page window treat an absent high-water value as `window.lo`, and never commit below `from`. `from` is safe as a floor, because a row read in the window held a value at or above `from`, and under invariant 2 its update is at or above that. No test covers either case; the fix wants one for each. It earns a delta review wherever it lands.

Nits (none changes correctness or the contract of what is reachable today):

- **N1. The new remedy cannot be followed on this head.** A mapping with `datasourceSource` parses, `os validate` warns that nothing reads it yet (`packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json`), and a pull of it is refused with `no_connector_source`, which tells the author to add a `connectorSource`, the key the two sources exclude each other on. The sentence it replaces named a retired mechanism and could not be followed either, so the net effect on the contract is nil, and the changeset says no such mapping is pulled by this release. It becomes a real defect if a release ships this changeset before the slice that wires `job.pull`. Carrier: the wiring slice lands before that release; see ③ 3.
- **N2. The error carries whole rows, and the ADR says watermark values.** D2: the error carries "the returned row count and each returned row's watermark value". `returnedValuesOf(field)` answers any column of up to cap + 1 rows as the driver returned them, before the floor's in-memory `where` is applied, so it can include rows the read's own predicates would have dropped. The reason is sound (the floor does not know which field is the watermark) and the reach is in-process callers holding the error instance. It is still wider than the ADR's letter and it sits on a root-exported class: record it as an accepted deviation in a dated ADR-0153 note, or narrow it when the wiring slice can tell the floor the field. A retained error also keeps those rows alive.
- **N3. An unreadable watermark in an over-cap answer is named `sync_bounds_not_pushed`.** `judgeBounds` treats any value `canonOf` cannot read as outside the window. For NULL that is right. For junk in a date or datetime column the same value in an under-cap answer is `watermark_not_exact`; over the cap the driver is blamed for a data problem.
- **N4. `pull-refusal.ts` says a caller of `IAutomationService.pullConnectorSource` branches on this one type for both sources.** True of the connector source only until the wiring slice; the sentence describes the next slice.
- **N5.** The over-declared lines, accepted in ②.

Tests read, not run: the listed ADR cases this slice can run are present on the path they name (interrupted after page one, the row behind the key cursor, 5000 / 5400 / 6200 on both paths, more rows than a page in one millisecond, the 64-bit key and watermark on SQLite, the .9996 floor), each refusal asserts `code`, `status` and `reason`, and the floor test asserts the payload is absent from `details`, own keys and a serialization. `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8 are `success` on this head.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · head `011f9aa4` · 2026-11-10T17:46Z · card #32062 (slice 1 of the P2 engine; `Part of`, the card stays open)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #32062`, and no closing keyword beside any card number. Eight files in `packages/objectql` (external-driver floor and error) and `packages/services/service-automation` (the windowed reader, the refusal module, the `connector-pull.ts` move), plus the changeset. Nothing under `packages/spec` differs from `main`.
- **Contract review:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on this head, record 6774735605. No must-fix. **S1 (should-fix)** is a hole in invariant 9: an absent or below-`from` high-water reading on a multi-page window commits uncapped or below `from`. It is not reachable on this head, because nothing calls the reader. It is carried as a **required item of slice 2**, the slice that wires the reader to `job.pull`, and earns its delta review there. Nits N1–N5 are accepted as recorded; N1–N4 ride slice 2 as listed on the card.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the card's lines. The review judges them a conservative over-declaration for this slice, honest by the changeset's own words (N5), and the level is `minor` on both packages.
- **Conflict merge:** one file (`connector-pull.ts`). Main's `mapping_name_refused` reason (#32117) was carried into the moved union, and the review confirmed it (① 5).
- **Gates:** CI on `011f9aa4`: 35 success · 16 skipped · 0 failed. The dev's local readings: objectql 12062 tests and service-automation 3594 tests pass, typechecks exit 0, ratchet families exit 0, and the dogfood battery on `647ec91d` reports VERDICT command-exit 0.
- **Release note for the maintainer (N1):** the changeset re-points `ExternalRowCapExceededError`'s remedy to sync-in, which cannot be followed until slice 2 wires `job.pull`. The seat keeps slice 2 ahead of anything else on this card.
- **Landing:** non-governed, 1383 lines ≤ 3000, K = 12, `mergeable_state` clean (merge-tree clean against `origin/main`). Ready + auto-merge.
